answer: Split each task into three parts for three random identities, so none sees all. Each part carries an umber hash-stamp linking it to the previous part; a verifier checks it before paying. The fable of one operator running three workshops collapses: clones must solve all three parts, tripling work per claim. In an ocean of look-alike claims, the chain makes each traceable; a break freezes all three rewards. One fake claim costs 45 minutes (3x15); 100 fakes cost 75 hours at $2/hour, $150, versus $100 of rewards, a $50 loss. Like a three-strand rope, it holds only if the strands are separate.
